sentences.text: If you swap the steel spring under a car for a rubber bag of air, you have air suspension.
But the bag leaks and goes flat, so the car sags down onto its tire.
Now over 4000 pounds of car press down on a flat bag that cannot hold it.
So you add a compressor that pumps air down a hose into the bag, and the car lifts.
But the little pump is slow, so after every dip the car stays low.
So you add a tank that stores pressurized air, and the bag refills in seconds.
But with nothing to stop the air, it rushes in, the bag swells, and the car shoots up too high.
So you add a valve that lets air in or out, and the car settles at the right height.
This bag is called an air spring.
And the bag, pump, tank and valve together are called air suspension.
The bag at about 100 psi lifts roughly 2800 pounds, though real bags give a bit less.
The compressor fills the tank, the valve opens, air lifts the car, then the valve lets it drops.
And air suspension is not only for show cars.
Buses and ambulances ride on air springs, and about three-quarters of new semi trailers use them.
Add a remote with a height button and a pressure light, then park the car rolling in.
Congratulations, you have built a bagged car.
